# Watch topics

Standing topics for the continuous-S4 loop. Each topic is a researcher dispatch when its cadence elapses.

Format per topic:
- **slug** — used in output path (`reports/<date>/<slug>.md`) and state-file keying. Lowercase, hyphenated, ≤40 chars.
- **cadence** — `daily` / `weekly` / `monthly` / `quarterly` / `paused`.
- **budget** — target line count for the report (researcher persona enforces ≤2× before escalating).
- **scope** — one-paragraph framing the researcher gets at dispatch time.
- **seed sources** — 3–5 URLs / paper IDs / GitHub repos / search queries for the researcher to anchor on.
- **notes** — operator-side context the researcher should know (priors, calibration, what's already covered elsewhere).

Topics are hand-curated. Workers do not edit this file (D2). Adding/removing/pausing happens via the operator or Orchestrator with explicit ratification.

**Brief corrections (T-2614):** if a researcher discovers during a dispatch that THIS topic's own brief — scope, seed sources, or notes — is wrong or stale, it emits a `brief_corrections:` frontmatter list on its report (a plain list of one-line strings) instead of only noting it in prose. `tools/watch_runner.py` carries any un-cleared entries into the NEXT cycle's brief for that topic automatically, so the defect can't be silently re-discovered. It does NOT edit this file — after folding a correction in by hand, clear it via `python3 tools/watch_runner.py --clear-correction --topic <slug> --id <id>` (ids/text are visible in the carried-forward brief section, or in `~/.local/state/pantheon/watch/state.json`'s `brief_corrections` key).

---

## llm-agent-failure-modes-research

- **cadence:** weekly
- **budget:** 500 lines
- **scope:** New peer-reviewed papers, technical reports, or industry post-mortems on multi-agent or single-agent LLM failure modes. Empirical findings preferred over theoretical. Cross-validate against MAST taxonomy (arXiv 2503.13657) and Huang et al. (arXiv 2408.00989) which are Pantheon's prior anchors.
- **seed sources:**
  - arXiv search: `cs.AI multi-agent LLM failure` (last month)
  - arXiv search: `cs.AI agent benchmark failure` (last month)
  - Anthropic engineering blog
  - OpenAI research blog
  - Google search: `multi-agent failure mode 2026` (filter recent)
- **notes:** distinguish primary research (papers, vendor data with methodology) from blog opinion. Tag `[weak]` for vendor-marketing throughput claims like Symphony's "500% PR" that aren't source-traceable. **Source-hygiene (added 2026-08-06 per T-2509):** `coasty.ai` is VENDOR-CONFLICTED — its companion posts claim ~82% for coasty's own product against OpenAI's 38%, and the domain shows content-farm characteristics (7+ near-duplicate SEO posts on one benchmark); it recurred as a citation 5× across 4 reports in this lane. General rule: when a vendor blog reports a *competitor's* benchmark number, cite the primary disclosure instead (e.g. OpenAI's own CUA numbers: 38.1% OSWorld success / 72.36% human baseline / 369 tasks), not the party that wins the comparison.

## mcp-supply-chain

- **cadence:** weekly
- **budget:** 250 lines
- **scope:** Security advisories, new high-traffic MCP servers entering the ecosystem, supply-chain incidents (rugpulls, post-trust modifications, credential exfiltration), CVEs against MCP clients (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) or popular servers.
- **seed sources:**
  - `https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/releases`
  - `https://owasp.org/www-project-mcp-top-10/` (updates)
  - `https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/search/results?query=MCP` (CVE filter)
  - OSV direct malware feeds (credential-free): `https://storage.googleapis.com/osv-vulnerabilities/npm/modified_id.csv` and `https://storage.googleapis.com/osv-vulnerabilities/PyPI/modified_id.csv`; fetch each retained record from the same ecosystem path as `<MAL-id>.json`
  - HN/Reddit: search `MCP server vulnerability` recent
- **notes:** the Postmark MCP rugpull (Sept 2025) and Anthropic MCP RCE (April 2026) are the prior anchors. Any new incident in this class is above-the-bar for the digest. **Standing malware-feed instrument (T-4253):** each week stream both OSV `modified_id.csv` feeds newest-first with a small overlap around the UTC report window; retain `MAL-` ids whose CSV timestamp reaches the window, fetch their JSON records, then keep records published or modified in-window whose package name matches `mcp|agent|claude|cursor|copilot|skill|llm|codex|gemini|openai|anthropic|model-context`. Treat a non-null `withdrawn` value as a retraction/update, deduplicate by id + ecosystem + package, and cite the record URL. OSV `/v1/query` is package-scoped and is not an ecosystem enumerator. The GitHub global-advisories API (`type=malware`, ecosystem + published/modified window, `per_page=100`, follow `Link: rel="next"`) is the fallback only; unauthenticated use has a shared 60/hour ceiling, and adding a token is a separate credential decision. **CVE-volume method (T-4254):** deduplicate CVE ids, group by project before week-over-week comparison, and report `N CVEs across M projects; largest single-project batch: X`. Report both raw and batch-adjusted volume; exclude a single-project batch from the spike/trend signal when its publication timing and patch history show a backlog assignment rather than a current cross-ecosystem wave, and state that rationale plus the batch's publication window and fixed-version status. Keep the batch's individual severity and Pantheon-exposure findings in the report—the adjustment changes only the aggregate trend interpretation.

  - **RESOLVED — do NOT re-flag `operating_point` (T-1778, orchestrator 2026-07-15):** the Speechmatics `operating_point`→`model` migration LANDED 2026-07 as a **wire-only serde rename** (serde rename to `model` on `TranscriptionConfig`, `types.rs` ~129; T-1563 / PR 198). Every INTERNAL symbol deliberately keeps the `operating_point` name (in-code decision doc), so a symbol-presence grep stays true FOREVER and false-fired twice (07-06 + 07-13 reports → duplicate T-1715, closed dup of T-1563). - **scope:** Monitor OTHER people building a system similar to the Grand Goal (ORG-053: a user-owned, model/device-portable, agentic, identity-continuous "living companion"). EMPHASIS on SMALL GROUPS AND INDIVIDUALS caught EARLY — new repos, indie launches, solo builders, seed-stage teams — NOT just big labs (those are covered by `agentic-harness-landscape` and `anthropic-claude-code-changelog`). Detection signature: flag anyone combining **2+ of** — (a) user-owned / self-hosted, (b) portable memory that survives a model OR device swap, (c) real agency (takes actions, not just chat), (d) persistent identity / continuity across sessions, (e) "grows / develops / living / companion" framing. Named tracked comparators (operator-approved 2026-08-10): **OpenClaw** (closest overall structural match) and **Hermes Agent (Nous)**. Report per player: what they have, which 2+ signals they hit, how close to ORG-053's shape, and momentum (stars/commits/funding/community growth); and how they FRAME the category / their narrative positioning (what "personal AI agent" means in their telling) — Pantheon needs awareness of the category-perception they're shaping.
- **seed sources:**
  - GitHub trending + new repos — queries: `agent memory portable`, `personal AI companion self-hosted`, `agent identity continuity`, `living AI agent`; topics `https://github.com/topics/personal-ai`, `https://github.com/topics/ai-companion`, `https://github.com/topics/agent-memory`
  - arXiv (agent memory / continuity / artificial-life): `https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent` + queries "lifelong agent memory", "persistent agent identity", "artificial life agent"
  - Show HN + Hacker News: `https://hn.algolia.com/?query=personal%20AI%20agent%20memory&sort=byDate` and Show HN launches
  - X / indie-hacker launches, Product Hunt AI-agent launches, small seed-round announcements
  - Prior comparators to keep tracking from the baseline: Letta, mem0 / OpenMemory, Khoj, Personal.ai, academic OpenLife
  - Funding and business news for each named tracked comparator (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent / Nous) and the baseline comparators: a dated news search per comparator each run (e.g. `"<name>" funding OR raises OR "Series" OR acquisition OR partnership`, past 7 days), corroborated against a primary source (company post, filing, or law-firm/investor announcement). GitHub metadata alone misses these: the 2026-10-12 and 10-19 reports missed Nous's $90M Series B of 2026-10-07 (T-5429).
- **notes:** Baseline established 2026-08-10 — `knowledge/episodic/2026-08-10-grand-goal-competitor-landscape/` (3-segment, ~20 players) + `knowledge/episodic/2026-08-10-hermes-nous-pantheon-threat-assessment/`. This is the GO-FORWARD standing coverage with the early/individual lens. Deliberately distinct from `agentic-harness-landscape` (which tracks the already-mapped MAJOR harnesses incl. OpenClaw + Hermes at the big-project level) — focus the delta on new/individual entrants, don't re-report the same big-lab items. **HERMES-discipline:** OpenClaw + Hermes are in Anthropic's classifier-scanned harness class — any dispatch/report touching them applies the byte-sequence escaping discipline in committed report content (escape the HERMES\.md filename byte sequence; OpenClaw is accept-and-monitor, referenced plain). Science-team owns weekly dispatch execution now that the topic exists.

## glop-it-blog

- **cadence:** weekly
- **budget:** 150 lines
- **scope:** Monitor https://glop.it/blog for NEW posts published in the past week. For each new post: title, publish date, a 2-3 sentence gist, and the link. If nothing new since the last dispatch, say so in one line (do not pad). Keep it a change-report, not an essay.
- **seed sources:**
  - `https://glop.it/blog` (the target blog; "Glop" is a blogging platform, this is the blog view)
  - ⚠ JS-rendered SPA — as of 2026-09-19 there is NO RSS/Atom at the usual paths (`/feed`, `/blog/feed`, `/feed.xml`, `/rss` all 404). The researcher likely needs to find the JSON/content API the page calls (inspect the SPA's XHR, e.g. an `/api/...` posts endpoint) or render the page, rather than plain-fetching the HTML (which returns only a "Loading posts…" shell).
- **notes:** operator-requested weekly monitor (TG 2026-09-19, msg 2222). The FIRST dispatch should establish a baseline snapshot (the set of posts that exist now + their dates) so subsequent weeks can diff for "new since last week" — record that baseline in the report so the next cycle has an anchor. No account/auth needed; it's a public blog.

This is a DELTA report: what arrived or changed in the past week, not a full re-survey. For each notable model give a usability verdict, not just news: capability tier (vs current frontier), access (free tier / open weights / cheap paid + $/M), context window, tool-calling / agentic support, and HARNESS FIT for us (drops into Codex CLI natively? Claude-Code-via-router? local via Ollama/vLLM?). Flag governance (hosted-provider data retention) and the local ceiling (our A2000 is 12 GB). System-one/typed-decision router priors: `knowledge/episodic/2026-09-19-jev-cua-s1-small-router-models/README.md` (JEV + CUA-S1). Pantheon use-lens: our harnesses are Claude Code (needs a LiteLLM/router shim for OpenAI-compatible backends) + Codex CLI (native OpenRouter). Governance: hosted providers retain prompts (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash / most OpenRouter routes) → non-sensitive/coding use only; only local is fully private. ## flipper-one-launch-watch

- **cadence:** daily
- **budget:** 120 lines
- **scope:** Launch watch for the Flipper One (Flipper Devices' RK3576 Linux networking multi-tool). Report only what changed since the last dispatch: a crowdfunding campaign (Kickstarter or other) or preorder page going live or getting a date, early-bird tiers and their prices and remaining quantities, the final spec sheet, ship-date estimates, and anything affecting availability (supply, regulatory, regional limits). If nothing changed, say so in one line. Set `surface: above-bar` when a campaign or preorder is live or dated, when early-bird pricing is published, or when the spec changes something in the fit analysis; otherwise `routine`.
- **seed sources:**
  - `https://flipper.net/pages/flipper-one` (official product page; was rate-limited on 2026-10-20, retry rather than skip)
  - `https://blog.flipper.net/` and `https://docs.flipper.net/one` (official blog + developer portal, which links a weekly developer newsletter)
  - Flipper Devices socials: X `@flipper_zero`, `https://www.youtube.com/@FlipperDevices`, `https://forum.flipper.net/`, `https://www.reddit.com/r/flipperzero/`
  - `https://www.kickstarter.com/` search `Flipper One` (Flipper Zero launched on Kickstarter in 2020)
- **notes:** operator-requested (TG 4727, 2026-10-20). He holds a reservation; per the operator TG 4789 (2026-10-28), all existing reservation coupons are grandfathered to the lower $379 price, so a new $379 coupon is not an upgrade for him and comparisons must use $379 rather than the batch's original sticker price. The job is to catch the Kickstarter the day it opens, before genuinely cheaper tiers sell out; that is why it is daily. Flipper sells numbered pre-order batches on flipper.net: a small paid ticket that reserves a launch price for the Kickstarter (the operator TG 4733), so a new batch, a batch closing, or a launch date are findings too. Fit analysis and reported specs: `sseed-presence/notes/2026-10-20-flipper-one-analysis.md`; only flag what is new against it. Tag press-only spec claims `[press]` until the official page confirms them. Retire this topic once the operator has ordered at a campaign tier or says to stop.

## Report output convention (read by `tools/watch_digest.py`)

Each report **begins with a frontmatter block** that the end-of-day digest reads to decide what to surface to the operator (the digest keys on this — it does NOT re-scan the report body; that's the P1 structural-surfacing design, replacing the old keyword heuristic):

```
---
surface: above-bar | routine
headline: <one line — the report's whole signal in the digest>
---
```

`surface: above-bar` is for genuinely operator-noteworthy findings only (new CVE / supply-chain / billing-or-policy change affecting Pantheon, a breaking change to a tool we run, a landscape shift that changes a prior verdict). `surface: routine` is the common, correct case for "nothing material this week" — do not inflate. The researcher emits this at report time (it has the full context); `tools/watch_runner.py:build_brief` instructs it.
